{
  "decision": "PROMOTE",
  "why": "FINAL decision for canary D (shop service 1.1). This file is self-contained; disregard earlier drafts of it from this session.

EVIDENCE (from the dashboard: 120 s load test, 80 req/s, 9788 requests; canary 2384 reqs ~= 24% of traffic, consistent with 1 canary pod behind the same Service as 3 stable pods):
- Errors: canary 0 5xx / 0.00% err; stable 0 5xx / 0.00% err. No error-rate regression on any route.
- Aggregate latency: canary p50 33 ms vs stable 35 ms; canary p95 95 ms vs stable 95 ms. Canary is equal or marginally better at p50 and p95.
- Per-route p50/p95 track stable closely: /browse 22/27 vs 22/27; /search 47/60 vs 47/59; /checkout 79/102 vs 82/103 (canary slightly faster on checkout).
- /checkout, the revenue path, is clean at every reported percentile including p99 (canary 105 ms vs stable 106 ms) with 0 5xx over 465 canary requests.
- Over time: canary p95 stays 92-95 ms across all four 30 s windows vs stable 93-97 ms, with 0 5xx in every window on both arms. No warm-up cliff, no drift, no degradation as the test progressed.
- Single anomaly: canary /search p99 = 652 ms vs stable 61 ms. This is what lifts canary aggregate p99 to 172 ms vs stable 104 ms.

JUDGEMENT (my reasoning, not measured fact):
- The /search p99 is computed over only 729 canary requests, so it is set by roughly the 7 slowest requests. Canary /search p95 is 60 ms against stable 59 ms, so the slow tail is confined to under 5% of search requests and, since p99 is the first percentile that moves at all, plausibly to well under 1%. A tail that thin, with p50 and p95 unchanged, zero errors, and no trend across four time windows, reads as a handful of outliers (GC pause, cold cache, scheduling noise on a single pod) rather than a systemic regression in 1.1.
- Cost asymmetry: a bad promote hurts customers, so I weighted the customer-facing signals hardest - 5xx rate, checkout latency, and stability over time. All three are clean. The residual risk is a few slow search responses, which degrade gracefully (a slow page, not an error and not a failed purchase).
- Honest limitation: one canary pod over 120 s gives weak statistical power at p99, so I cannot prove the 652 ms is noise. That is why promotion is paired with monitoring rather than treated as closed. If the same 652 ms p99 had appeared on /checkout, or alongside any non-zero 5xx, I would have rolled back instead.

PLAN ON PROMOTE: shift 1.1 to 100%, keep the 1.0 image ready for immediate rollback, and watch /search specifically for 15-30 min at full traffic, where the sample size makes p99 meaningful. Roll back if /search p99 stays above ~200 ms, if /search p95 rises above its 59-60 ms baseline, or on any non-zero 5xx rate."
}

Basis (evidence from the supplied dashboard; 120 s, 80 req/s, 9788 requests):
- Zero 5xx on both arms, overall and per endpoint: stable 0/7404, canary 0/2384, 0.00% err everywhere.

Worst case implied is ~1% of searches at ~650 ms: slow, not broken.

Judgement on the trade-off: the customer-harm channels named in the goal (errors, checkout latency) are clean, so this does not meet the bar for blocking the release. Promote, but monitor /search p99 after the cutover — 4x the traffic is the real test of whether that tail was noise or a thin slow path; roll back if p95 or error rate moves.
